intro: Two measurements can move together even when their means are very different. Center the observations to reveal that relationship.
task: Return the sample covariance matrix for observations stored as rows and features stored as columns.
requirements: X is a finite matrix with at least two rows and at least one feature.
Center each feature and divide the outer-product sum by n - 1 (ddof=1).
Return a NumPy array of shape (d, d), including (1, 1) for one feature.
Do not modify inputs. Raise ValueError for the invalid shapes, ranges, or non-finite numeric inputs described above. Numerical checks use moderate finite values unless stated otherwise.

examples.name: Positive relationship
examples.output:
[[2.0, 2.0], [2.0, 2.0]]
(Numeric values rounded to 8 decimal places where needed.)

examples.name: Opposing movement
examples.output:
[[1.0, -1.0], [-1.0, 1.0]]
(Numeric values rounded to 8 decimal places where needed.)

examples.name: One feature remains a matrix
examples.output:
[[4.0]]
(Numeric values rounded to 8 decimal places where needed.)

hints.title: Choose the representation
hints.body: Subtract X.mean(axis=0), then multiply centered.T by centered.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Keep the two-dimensional matrix shape when d equals one; do not squeeze.

explanation: Covariance describes joint variation around feature means. A positive off-diagonal entry means above-average values tend to occur together; a negative entry indicates opposing movement.
Rows are observations, so the centered transpose times the centered matrix has feature-by-feature shape. The n - 1 denominator is the requested sample estimator.
Add a different constant to every feature and compare the matrices. Then rescale one feature: covariance changes with units, which is why covariance and correlation answer different questions.
